questions.question: In which year did Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar lead the Mahad Satyagraha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1927**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mahad Satyagraha was led by Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar in **1927** to fight for the rights of Dalits to access public water sources.
 
• The movement took place in Mahad, a town in the present-day Raigad district of Maharashtra.
 
• The primary objective was to allow Dalits to drink water from the Chavdar Tank, which was previously restricted to upper castes.
 
• It was a landmark event in the **Dalit rights movement** and highlighted the practice of untouchability in India.
 
• Ambedkar publicly burned the **Manusmriti** during the protest, symbolizing his rejection of caste-based discrimination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Untouchability:** A social practice in India where certain communities, primarily Dalits, were ostracized and denied access to basic rights and resources.
 
• **Manusmriti:** An ancient Hindu legal text that endorsed caste-based discrimination, which Ambedkar burned as a symbolic act during the Mahad Satyagraha.
 
• **Dalit Rights Movement:** A series of protests and reforms led by leaders like Ambedkar to fight against caste-based oppression and secure equal rights for Dalits.
 
• **Chavdar Tank:** A public water tank in Mahad, Maharashtra, that became the focal point of the Mahad Satyagraha.
 
• **Impact of Mahad Satyagraha:** The movement was a turning point in India's social reform, challenging the caste system and advocating equality and justice.

questions.question: The Boilers Bill, 2024, introduced in Rajya Sabha on 8 August 2024, seeks to replace which previous Boilers Act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Boilers Act, 1923**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Boilers Bill, 2024, introduced in the Rajya Sabha on 8 August 2024, seeks to replace the **Boilers Act, 1923**, which has been in place for over a century.
 
• The Boilers Act, 1923, regulated the operation, inspection, and certification of boilers used in industries to ensure safety and efficiency.
 
• The Bill aims to modernize boiler regulations, addressing advancements in technology, safety standards, and industrial practices.
 
• It incorporates stricter safety norms and compliance measures to prevent boiler-related accidents and enhance energy efficiency.
 
• This initiative is part of the government's broader agenda to reform outdated legislation and align industrial practices with global standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boilers Act, 1923:**

 
 
• Enacted to regulate the safety of boilers in industries to prevent accidents caused by steam pressure.
 
• Mandated periodic inspections and certifications of boilers by authorized inspectors.
 
• Defined penalties for non-compliance with safety standards.
 
 
 
• **Boiler:**
 
 
• A boiler is a closed vessel used for generating steam or heating water under pressure, typically used in industries like power generation, textile, and manufacturing.
 
• Boiler safety is critical as failures can lead to catastrophic accidents, loss of life, and property damage.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Safety Reforms:**
 
 
• The modernization of boiler regulations is part of India’s focus on enhancing workplace safety and operational efficiency.
 
• It aligns with global standards such as ISO 16528 for boiler and pressure vessel safety.
 
 
 
• **Key Technological Advancements:**
 
 
• Modern boilers now incorporate advanced automation, monitoring systems, and energy-efficient designs to improve safety and performance.
 
• The new legislation is expected to mandate the adoption of such technologies in industrial boilers.

questions.question: 'Streets Of Calcutta' and 'Dancing Drums' are the two popular tracks of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ananda Shankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ananda Shankar** was a renowned Indian musician known for blending Indian classical music with Western rock and electronic music.
 
• The tracks **'Streets of Calcutta'** and **'Dancing Drums'** are iconic pieces from his album released in the 1970s, showcasing his experimental fusion style.
 
• Ananda Shankar was the nephew of the legendary sitar virtuoso **Ravi Shankar**, but he carved his own niche in the global music scene.
 
• His work contributed significantly to the genre of world music, influencing generations of artists in both India and abroad.
 
• Ananda Shankar's music featured instruments like the sitar alongside synthesizers, creating a unique and groundbreaking sound.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Music:** A genre that combines traditional music from various cultures with modern elements, promoting cross-cultural musical exchange.
 
• **Fusion Music:** A style that blends multiple musical traditions, such as classical Indian music with Western pop, rock, or electronic genres.
 
• **Sitar:** A traditional Indian string instrument prominently used in Indian classical music and famously associated with Ravi Shankar.
 
• **Electronic Music:** A genre of music that uses electronic instruments, synthesizers, and digital technology for production and composition.
 
• Ananda Shankar's work has been featured in several international compilations, highlighting his contributions to experimental and world music.

questions.question: What impact did the Green Revolution have on India's dependence on food imports?

options.text: No change in dependence on food imports

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decreased dependence on food imports**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India, initiated in the 1960s, led to a significant increase in agricultural productivity, especially in the production of wheat and rice.
 
• It introduced high-yield variety (HYV) seeds, modern irrigation techniques, and chemical fertilizers, enabling self-sufficiency in food production.
 
• By the late 1970s, India transitioned from a food-deficient country to a food surplus nation, reducing its reliance on food imports.
 
• The Green Revolution helped India achieve food security, especially during times of population growth and economic challenges.
 
• It also played a critical role in alleviating famines and ensuring the availability of staple foods domestically, lessening external dependence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High-Yield Variety (HYV) Seeds:** These seeds were pivotal to the Green Revolution, offering higher productivity compared to traditional seeds, especially for crops like wheat and rice.
 
• **Role of Irrigation:** The expansion of irrigation infrastructure, such as canals and tube wells, ensured a consistent water supply, crucial for HYV seeds' success.
 
• **Fertilizers and Pesticides:** The increased use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides significantly boosted crop yields but also raised concerns about environmental impact.
 
• **Impact on Rural Economy:** While the Green Revolution increased incomes for many farmers, it also widened the gap between large and small landholders, leading to socio-economic disparities.
 
• **Food Security Achievements:** India’s improved agricultural output enabled the establishment of the Public Distribution System (PDS) and buffer stock management, ensuring food availability during crises.

questions.question: The Constituent Assembly met for the first time on:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9th December 1946**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Constituent Assembly of India met for the first time on **9th December 1946**, marking the beginning of the drafting process for India's Constitution.
 
• The meeting was held in the Constitution Hall (now known as the Central Hall of Parliament) in New Delhi.
 
• **Sachchidananda Sinha**, the oldest member of the Assembly, was appointed as the temporary President for the inaugural session.
 
• A total of **207 members** attended this first session out of 389 originally elected members, as representatives from Muslim League and princely states largely abstained.
 
• This date is considered pivotal in Indian history as it laid the foundation for the creation of the world's largest democracy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constituent Assembly:**

 
 
• It was formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946, sent by the British government to discuss the transfer of power.
 
• The Assembly had members from provinces and princely states, chosen via indirect elections.
 
• The main purpose of the Assembly was to draft the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• **Drafting Committee:**
 
 
• The Drafting Committee, chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, was formed on **29th August 1947**.
 
• The Constitution was adopted on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the First Session:**
 
 
• The first session set the tone for subsequent discussions and debates on the Constitution.
 
• It highlighted the challenges of uniting diverse interests, religions, and regions of India.
 
 
 
• **Constitution Hall:**
 
 
• The venue for the first session, the Constitution Hall, is now part of the Indian Parliament complex and symbolizes India’s journey to democracy.

questions.question: Which species of green algae, commonly known as stonewort, is often mistaken for a plant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chara** is a genus of green algae belonging to the Charophyta division and is commonly referred to as stonewort.
 
• It is often mistaken for a plant due to its complex morphology, including stem-like structures and whorls of branchlets.
 
• Chara is found predominantly in freshwater environments like ponds and lakes, where it grows submerged.
 
• Unlike vascular plants, Chara lacks true roots, stems, and leaves but has rhizoids for anchoring and nutrient absorption.
 
• Its body structure and reproductive mechanisms make it one of the closest relatives to land plants within the algal group.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charophytes:** A group of green algae that are the closest relatives to land plants, sharing similar cellular and reproductive structures.
 
• **Rhizoids:** Thread-like structures found in Chara that function similarly to roots, aiding in anchoring and nutrient absorption.
 
• **Stonewort:** The nickname "stonewort" comes from its calcified appearance due to the deposition of calcium carbonate on its surface.
 
• **Reproductive Structures:** Chara reproduces sexually using oogonia (female structures) and antheridia (male structures), which resemble plant reproductive organs.
 
• **Ecological Role:** Chara plays a vital role in aquatic ecosystems by oxygenating water, providing habitat for aquatic organisms, and stabilizing sediments.

questions.question: At room temperature and pressure, kinetic energy of the particles are minimum in case of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**iron**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• At room temperature and pressure, the particles in solids like **iron** have the least kinetic energy compared to liquids or gases.
 
• In solids, particles are tightly packed in a fixed lattice structure, which restricts their movement, minimizing their kinetic energy.
 
• **Iron**, being a solid, exhibits strong intermolecular forces, which further limits the motion of its particles.
 
• In contrast, gases like methane and liquids like water or kerosene have particles with higher kinetic energy due to weaker intermolecular forces and greater freedom of movement.
 
• The kinetic energy of particles is directly proportional to their motion, and in the case of solids, this motion is minimal (restricted to vibrations about a fixed position).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kinetic Energy in States of Matter**

 
 
• Kinetic energy refers to the energy of motion. The particles in solids have the least kinetic energy, while gases have the highest.
 
• In liquids, particles have more kinetic energy than solids but less than gases, allowing them to flow but not expand indefinitely.
 
 
 
• **Intermolecular Forces**
 
 
• Solids like iron have the strongest intermolecular forces, keeping particles in fixed positions.
 
• Liquids and gases have weaker intermolecular forces, which result in greater freedom of movement for their particles.
 
 
 
• **Particle Movement in Solids**
 
 
• In solids, particles vibrate around fixed points but do not move freely, resulting in low kinetic energy.
 
• This is why solids maintain a definite shape and volume, unlike liquids and gases.
 
 
 
• **Temperature and Kinetic Energy**
 
 
• Kinetic energy increases with temperature as particles gain more thermal energy.
 
• At room temperature, solids like iron remain in their low-energy state due to their rigid structure.

questions.question: Which of the following neighbouring countries of India has the highest number of million cities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pakistan has the highest number of million cities among India’s neighboring countries, with cities like Karachi, Lahore, Faisalabad, Rawalpindi, and others having populations exceeding one million.
 
• As per the latest data, Pakistan has over 10 cities with populations exceeding one million, making it the leader in this category among India's neighbors.
 
• Karachi, Pakistan's largest city, is not only the country's economic hub but also one of the most populous cities in the world.
 
• India's other neighboring countries, such as Nepal and Sri Lanka, have relatively smaller urban populations and fewer cities crossing the one million population mark.
 
• Bangladesh also has significant urban centers, like Dhaka and Chittagong, but fewer in number compared to Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Million Cities:** These are urban centers with populations exceeding one million. They are usually characterized by high economic activity, better infrastructure, and dense populations.
 
• **Karachi:** The largest city in Pakistan, it is a major port and industrial hub, contributing significantly to the country's GDP.
 
• **Urbanization in South Asia:** Countries like India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh are experiencing rapid urbanization, driven by economic opportunities and population growth.
 
• **Population Density in Neighboring Countries:** Bangladesh, despite having fewer million cities than Pakistan, is one of the most densely populated countries in the world.
 
• **Urban Planning Challenges:** Rapid growth in million cities leads to challenges such as housing shortages, traffic congestion, pollution, and strain on public services.

questions.question: 'Public provision' refers to those goods and services financed through the budget and:

options.text: can be used by taxpayers only
can be used only with direct payment
can be used without any direct payment
is available through online payment only

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**can be used without any direct payment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Public provision** refers to goods and services that are financed through government budgets and provided for public benefit.
 
• These goods and services can be accessed **without any direct payment** by the users at the point of use.
 
• Examples include public healthcare, public education, infrastructure, and subsidized services like public transportation.
 
• The cost of such provisions is covered through **tax revenues**, ensuring equitable access to essential services for all sections of society.
 
• This approach supports the government's role in promoting **social welfare and reducing inequality**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Goods:** Goods that are non-excludable and non-rivalrous, meaning they can be consumed by everyone without reducing their availability to others (e.g., street lighting, national defense).
 
• **Merit Goods:** Services considered beneficial for individuals and society, often provided by the government at low or no cost (e.g., education, healthcare).
 
• **Progressive Taxation:** A taxation system where higher-income groups pay a higher percentage of their income, ensuring funding for public provisions and reducing income inequality.
 
• **Subsidies:** Financial assistance provided by the government to reduce the cost of certain goods or services, making them affordable for the general public.
 
• **Welfare State:** A concept where the government takes responsibility for the well-being of its citizens by providing essential services and ensuring a minimum standard of living.

questions.question: Smriti Mandhana is associated with which of the following sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cricket**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Smriti Mandhana is a prominent Indian cricketer who plays for the Indian women's national team.
 
• She is known for her aggressive left-handed batting and is regarded as one of the finest batters in women's cricket globally.
 
• Mandhana was named the ICC Women's Cricketer of the Year in 2018 and won the Rachael Heyhoe Flint Award for the same.
 
• She has been a vital part of India's major cricket tournaments, including the ICC Women's World Cup and T20 World Cup.
 
• Smriti Mandhana is also a key player in domestic and franchise cricket, representing teams like Trailblazers in the Women's T20 Challenge and Southern Brave in The Hundred.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC Women's Cricketer of the Year:** This prestigious award is given annually by the International Cricket Council (ICC) to the best-performing female cricketer globally.
 
• **Women's T20 World Cup:** A major international cricket tournament organized by the ICC, where teams compete in the T20 format.
 
• **The Hundred:** An innovative franchise-based cricket league in England featuring 100-ball matches, where Smriti Mandhana has participated as a marquee player.
 
• **Women's T20 Challenge:** A domestic Indian cricket tournament that serves as the female equivalent of the IPL, aimed at promoting women's cricket.
 
• **Smriti Mandhana's Achievements:** She was the youngest T20I captain for India and has numerous centuries across formats, showcasing her consistency and skill in cricket.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT an outcome of the Green Revolution?

options.text: High dependency on chemical fertilisers and pesticides

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decrease in rural population**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Decrease in rural population** was not an outcome of the Green Revolution; the rural population remained largely stable during this period.
 
• The Green Revolution led to a significant **increase in food grain production**, particularly in wheat and rice, ensuring self-sufficiency in food for India.
 
• A key result of the Green Revolution was the **high dependency on chemical fertilizers and pesticides** to boost agricultural yields.
 
• It also promoted the development of **improved agricultural infrastructure**, including irrigation systems, roads, and storage facilities.
 
• The Green Revolution primarily benefited regions with access to irrigation, leading to regional disparities in agricultural growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:** A series of initiatives introduced in the mid-20th century to increase agricultural productivity in India using high-yield variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and advanced irrigation techniques.
 
• **High-Yield Variety Seeds:** These seeds were a cornerstone of the Green Revolution and significantly increased the production of wheat and rice.
 
• **Impact on Farmers:** While larger farmers benefitted significantly, small-scale farmers often struggled with the cost of fertilizers, pesticides, and machinery.
 
• **Environmental Effects:** The intensive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides led to soil degradation, water pollution, and reduced biodiversity in some areas.
 
• **Regional Disparities:** The Green Revolution had a limited impact on rain-fed areas and regions without proper irrigation infrastructure, such as eastern and southern India.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dances is known to be ekaharya, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam**, one of the oldest classical dance forms in India, is known for its unique feature of **Ekaharya**, where a single dancer portrays multiple characters in a single performance.
 
• The term **Ekaharya** derives from Sanskrit, meaning "one actor" or "one character," highlighting the versatility of the performer.
 
• This dance form uses intricate **abhinaya (expressive gestures)** and body movements to depict multiple roles, often supported by rich mythological narratives.
 
• Bharatanatyam, originating from Tamil Nadu, is deeply rooted in **Natya Shastra**, an ancient treatise on performing arts written by sage Bharata.
 
• It is a highly codified art form performed in temples as a form of devotion and later evolved into a stage performance art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Natya Shastra:**

 
 
• It is an ancient Indian treatise on performing arts attributed to sage Bharata, detailing various aspects of drama, dance, and music.
 
• It outlines the principles of Rasa (emotions), Abhinaya (expressions), and Mudras (gestures) used in Bharatanatyam.
 
 
 
• **Key Elements of Bharatanatyam:**
 
 
• **Nritta:** Pure dance movements without storytelling elements.
 
• **Nritya:** Expressive dance that conveys emotions and stories through gestures and facial expressions.
 
• **Natya:** Dramatic art, combining speech, music, and dance.
 
 
 
• **Ekaharya in Other Classical Dances:** While Bharatanatyam is prominent for Ekaharya, similar concepts can be seen in other forms like Kathak and Kuchipudi, though Bharatanatyam is most recognized for it.
 
• **Devadasi Tradition:** Historically, Bharatanatyam was performed by Devadasis (female temple dancers) as a form of devotion to deities in temples.
 
• **Modern Revival:** Bharatanatyam was revived and redefined as a stage art form in the 20th century by pioneers like Rukmini Devi Arundale.

questions.question: Who is the cabinet minister of the Union Ministry of Education, as of September 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharmendra Pradhan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dharmendra Pradhan is the **Union Cabinet Minister for Education** in the Government of India as of September 2024.
 
• He has held the position since **July 7, 2021**, after a cabinet reshuffle by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• In addition to education, Dharmendra Pradhan is also responsible for the **Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship**.
 
• He has played a pivotal role in implementing the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**, focusing on holistic and multidisciplinary education reforms.
 
• Previously, he served as the Minister of Petroleum and Natural Gas, where he was instrumental in initiatives like the **Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020:**

 
 
• The NEP 2020 aims to transform India's education system, emphasizing early childhood care, foundational literacy, and skill development.
 
• It introduces a **5+3+3+4 structure**, replacing the previous 10+2 structure, focusing on flexibility and multidisciplinary education.
 
• Key aspects include vocational training from Grade 6, increased use of regional languages, and fostering critical thinking.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Education:**
 
 
• Previously known as the Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD), it was renamed in **2020** under NEP reforms.
 
• The ministry is responsible for formulating policies to improve school and higher education in India.
 
 
 
• **Dharmendra Pradhan's Background:**
 
 
• He is a senior leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and hails from Odisha.
 
• He has a strong political career with extensive experience in governance and public administration.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship:**
 
 
• This ministry focuses on enhancing employability through skill training and entrepreneurship development initiatives.
 
• It collaborates with the education ministry for skill integration into formal education under the NEP.

questions.question: The last Shunga ruler was killed by his minister in which century?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1st century BC**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Shunga dynasty was established around **185 BCE** after the fall of the Maurya Empire by Pushyamitra Shunga.
 
• The last ruler of the Shunga dynasty, **Devabhuti**, was assassinated by his minister **Vasudeva Kanva**, marking the end of the dynasty.
 
• This event occurred in the **1st century BC**, around 73 BCE, leading to the rise of the Kanva dynasty.
 
• The Shunga dynasty ruled for nearly 112 years, focusing on the revival of Hinduism and promoting art and culture.
 
• Devabhuti's assassination signified a shift in political power to the Kanvas, who ruled until the Satavahanas took over.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shunga Dynasty:** It succeeded the Maurya Empire and is known for its contributions to Indian art, including the construction of stupas and sculptures at Bharhut and Sanchi.
 
• **Pushyamitra Shunga:** The founder of the Shunga dynasty, who played a key role in reviving Hindu practices after the Mauryan support of Buddhism.
 
• **Kanva Dynasty:** Founded by Vasudeva Kanva, this dynasty replaced the Shungas and ruled central India until the rise of the Satavahana dynasty.
 
• **Devabhuti:** The last Shunga ruler, known for his indulgent lifestyle, which eventually led to his assassination and the decline of the dynasty.
 
• **Political Transition:** The assassination of Devabhuti marked a period of political instability, paving the way for the Kanva dynasty and regional powers like the Satavahanas and Kushanas.

questions.question: Who among the following makes the rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the State government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor of the State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Governor of the State** is empowered to make rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the State Government under Article 166(3) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These rules specify the manner in which the executive business of the State is conducted and allocated among ministers.
 
• The Governor acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister in formulating these rules.
 
• The Governor’s role is largely formal and procedural, ensuring that the business of the State Government is carried out efficiently and constitutionally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 166 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• It deals with the conduct of business of the Government of a State.
 
• Article 166(1) states that all executive actions of the Government of a State shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor.
 
• Article 166(3) empowers the Governor to make rules for the convenient transaction of business of the State Government.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Chief Minister:**
 
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers and advises the Governor on various matters, including the formulation of rules for the business of the State.
 
• The Governor acts on this advice in accordance with constitutional provisions.
 
 
 
• **Advocate General of the State:**
 
 
• The Advocate General is the highest law officer of a State but does not have a role in making rules for the transaction of State Government business.
 
 
 
• **Chief Secretary of the State:**
 
 
• The Chief Secretary is the administrative head of the State Government and assists in the implementation of rules but does not create them.

questions.question: In which state is the Nandi Award for the best choreographer presented every year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

__
 
• The Nandi Awards are prestigious awards presented annually by the government of **Andhra Pradesh** to recognize excellence in Telugu cinema, theatre, and television.
 
• The award was instituted in **1964** and is considered one of the highest honors in the Telugu film industry.
 
• The Nandi Awards are named after the **Nandi (bull),** a cultural and historical symbol of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The Best Choreographer Award is among the many categories that honor exceptional contributions to Telugu cinema, including acting, directing, and technical excellence.
 
• The awards are typically announced by the Department of Information and Public Relations of the Andhra Pradesh government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Choreography:**

 
 
• Choreography refers to the art of designing sequences of movements, typically in dance, which are performed by artists in films, theatre, or other performances.
 
• Choreographers play a vital role in enhancing the visual appeal of songs and dance sequences in cinema.
 
 
 
• **Telugu Film Industry:**
 
 
• Also known as "Tollywood," it is one of the largest regional film industries in India, producing films in the Telugu language.
 
• It has a significant audience base in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and among the Telugu-speaking diaspora worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Other Nandi Award Categories:**
 
 
• Best Actor, Best Actress, Best Director, Best Screenplay, and Best Music Director, among others.
 
• Special awards like the Raghupathi Venkaiah Award are given for lifetime contributions to Telugu cinema.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Nandi Symbol:**
 
 
• The bull, Nandi, is associated with Lord Shiva and represents strength, loyalty, and cultural heritage in Hindu traditions.
 
• The award trophy features a depiction of Nandi as a mark of cultural pride for Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: Which of the following is a human-made water body created by blocking the flow of a river or stream?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reservoir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **reservoir** is a human-made water body created by constructing a dam to block the flow of a river or stream.
 
• Reservoirs are primarily built to store water for purposes such as irrigation, drinking water supply, hydroelectric power generation, and flood control.
 
• Famous examples include the **Bhakra Reservoir** (India) and the **Hoover Dam Reservoir** (USA).
 
• These artificial water bodies help in managing water resources and ensuring water availability during dry periods.
 
• Reservoirs also support aquatic ecosystems and recreational activities like fishing and boating.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lagoon:** A lagoon is a shallow water body separated from a larger water body, such as the sea, by a barrier like a sandbank or coral reef.
 
• **Estuary:** An estuary is a coastal area where freshwater from rivers mixes with saltwater from the ocean, creating a unique brackish environment.
 
• **Oxbow Lake:** This is a naturally formed water body created when a river meander is cut off from the main flow, forming a crescent-shaped lake.
 
• **Dam Construction:** The creation of reservoirs often involves building large dams, such as gravity dams, arch dams, or earthen dams, depending on geological and environmental conditions.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** While reservoirs provide significant benefits, they can also disrupt local ecosystems, displace communities, and affect sediment flow in rivers.

questions.question: The term 'Rohingya Crisis' primarily involves refugees from which neighbouring country seeking shelter in various regions, including India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Myanmar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rohingya Crisis primarily involves the **Rohingya Muslim minority** from Myanmar, who have faced persecution in their homeland.
 
• Myanmar's **Rakhine State** has been the epicenter of the crisis, where systematic violence and discrimination have led to mass displacement.
 
• In 2017, a military crackdown in Myanmar resulted in the exodus of over **740,000 Rohingya refugees** to neighboring countries like Bangladesh, India, Malaysia, and others.
 
• The Rohingya are considered **stateless** in Myanmar under the 1982 Citizenship Law, leaving them without legal rights and protections.
 
• The United Nations has described the violence against the Rohingya as a possible **genocide** and "ethnic cleansing."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rohingya Ethnicity:** The Rohingya are a primarily Muslim ethnic group with a distinct language and culture, differing from Myanmar's dominant Buddhist population.
 
• **Bangladesh's Role:** Bangladesh has been the primary host for Rohingya refugees, sheltering over 1 million individuals in camps such as **Cox's Bazar**, the world's largest refugee settlement.
 
• **International Response:** The crisis has drawn global attention, with the **International Court of Justice (ICJ)** conducting hearings on alleged genocide and various nations providing humanitarian aid.
 
• **Impact on India:** India has received thousands of Rohingya refugees, though their presence has sparked debates on national security, border management, and humanitarian obligations.
 
• **UNHCR Involvement:** The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) plays a key role in providing support, documentation, and advocacy for the rights of Rohingya refugees.

questions.question: Which festival from West Bengal has found a place in the UNESCO list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Durga Puja**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Durga Puja**, a major Hindu festival celebrated in West Bengal, was inscribed on the **UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity** in December 2021.
 
• It is recognized for its **rich cultural traditions, artistic expressions, and community participation** that transcend religious boundaries.
 
• The festival involves intricate idol-making, vibrant processions, cultural performances, and traditional rituals, showcasing the **creative and spiritual heritage of Bengal**.
 
• Durga Puja is celebrated annually during the autumn season and honors the victory of Goddess Durga over the demon Mahishasura.
 
• The recognition by UNESCO highlights the festival's **global cultural significance** and its role in fostering social cohesion and cultural diversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage:**

 
 
• Established in 2003, this list aims to safeguard practices, representations, expressions, knowledge, and skills that communities recognize as part of their cultural heritage.
 
• India has several elements inscribed on this list, including Yoga, Kumbh Mela, and now Durga Puja.
 
 
 
• **Durga Puja Celebrations:**
 
 
• It spans over 10 days, with the last five days being the most significant, including **Shashthi, Saptami, Ashtami, Navami, and Dashami.**
 
• Dashami marks the immersion of the Durga idols, symbolizing the return of the goddess to her celestial abode.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• Durga Puja generates significant economic activity, especially in Kolkata, with expenditures on pandals, decorations, cultural programs, and food.
 
• It also serves as a source of livelihood for artisans, craftsmen, and workers involved in the festival.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO and India:**
 
 
• India has 14 intangible cultural heritage elements inscribed on the UNESCO list as of 2023.
 
• This recognition enhances global awareness of India's rich cultural traditions and promotes tourism.
